subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Draft direction is sound but needs two structural refinements. Tests must parse Markdown frontmatter separately from prompt bodies: exact MCP permission keys are executable OpenCode configuration, while concrete invocation syntax in prose is the portability defect. Contract coverage and token-budget checks should follow deployed/assembled prompt ownership rather than require duplicate text in every raw command/agent/overlay file. OpenCode's CodeMode runtime already owns catalog and instruction generation, so Advance should remove the speculative runtime-hook/OpenCode-patch branch from the baseline design and reopen it only on reproducible validation failure. Candidates, sorted by payoff/risk: (1) auto-adopt — frontmatter/body-aware scanner; payoff high, risk low, ties dual-mode operation and no false availability, fate design_around; (2) auto-adopt — test deployment-owned effective prompt surfaces and <=100-token Advance guidance once per assembled surface, not raw-file duplication; payoff high, risk low, ties overhead and overlay/deploy parity, fate design_around; (3) auto-adopt — make no runtime hook/patch the closed baseline and require explicit failing dual-mode fixture before scope re-entry; payoff medium, risk low, ties OpenCode catalog ownership and avoidance, fate adopt_now; (4) surface — run toolbox wrapper fix in parallel and keep Advance acceptance evidence independent through clean-environment direct-schema and CodeMode fixtures, then add wrapper evidence when linked change lands; payoff medium, risk medium, ties cross-repo tracking and both modes, fate surface_to_user. Candidate 2 remains partly uncertain because official command documentation confirms command-body prompt ownership but does not explicitly document full agent-plus-command prompt composition; I don't know whether one agent-level contract is always inherited by every command path.

validation.notes: No design blocker. Caution: an unconditional raw-text ban can break legitimate exact tool permission keys, and per-file contract requirements can violate the <=100-token assembled-prompt constraint through duplication.

tradeoffs: Frontmatter/body-aware checks are slightly more code than a repository-wide regex but prevent false positives against executable OpenCode permission keys.
Effective-prompt parity tests reduce duplicate guidance but require a small, explicit model of deploy/overlay ownership.
Keeping wrapper work parallel preserves cross-repo boundaries but requires acceptance evidence to distinguish Advance correctness from toolbox launch-environment correctness.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Core architecture is correct and least-coupled: OpenCode source proves CodeMode owns generated paths/catalog text, suppresses execute when no permission-visible MCP tools exist, and omits direct MCP tools when CodeMode is active; direct mode exposes exact MCP keys. Advance should therefore remove unconditional callable spellings and add one mode-neutral active-surface rule, without a translation hook or OpenCode patch (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/05c3e40a4e641732b991499000ca479e5dad4b02/packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts#L277-L304; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/05c3e40a4e641732b991499000ca479e5dad4b02/packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts#L387-L439). Three design details need tightening: AC6 needs a deterministic assembled-prompt baseline and tokenizer/model-token policy because current Advance tests count lines only (file:///home/jon/dev/advance/plugin/src/adv-skill-backed-commands-assets.test.ts#L797-L858); active-prose scanning must recurse through all deployed prompt-bearing skill files because deployment copies whole skill directories (file:///home/jon/dev/advance/scripts/deploy-local.sh#L1488-L1515); and DDC5 must enumerate mandatory primary plus spawned researcher cases rather than qualify them as 'where applicable' (adv://updateCodemodeMcpContracts/agreement#AC1).

validation.notes: No architectural blocker. Before design completion, specify (1) exact pre-change assembled-prompt fixtures and deterministic token counting for AC6, (2) a manifest-driven recursive active prompt corpus including skill sibling/reference files while excluding archive, and (3) an explicit required runtime matrix preserving AC1 primary and spawned-researcher cases. Target spec-law review is limited to the approved strict contract because the target-routed spec tool is unavailable.

tradeoffs: One compact policy reduces stale syntax and catalog duplication, but still requires deliberate placement across independently assembled agent surfaces (file:///home/jon/dev/advance/scripts/deploy-local.sh#L1400-L1450).

Capability-oriented prose is durable across modes, but loses copy-paste callable examples; OpenCode's generated catalog/direct schema must supply exact syntax (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/05c3e40a4e641732b991499000ca479e5dad4b02/packages/opencode/src/tool/code-mode.ts#L39-L65).

Manifest-driven recursive scanning gives stronger coverage, but needs explicit classification for configuration/frontmatter, executable prompt prose, documentation, fixtures, and archives (file:///home/jon/dev/advance/plugin/src/tool-name-assets.test.ts#L39-L81).

## Cross-Project Origin

This change was created as a follow-up from **toolbox** change `updateMcpDefaults` after CodeMode was enabled by default in the `oc` wrapper. User reconfirmed this lineage during discovery.

# Update CodeMode MCP contracts

## Why

Advance’s MCP invocation guidance may conflict with OpenCode CodeMode, but the best ecosystem-wide response is unknown. Advance currently embeds direct MCP-call examples and exact-name constraints in durable prompts. CodeMode replaces direct MCP exposure with an `execute` catalog, while Advance plugin tools and built-ins remain top-level. A broad rewrite could restore compatibility but also duplicate OpenCode-owned runtime knowledge, increase prompt complexity, and create another synchronization burden.

This change must establish the best shape through source-backed investigation and representative runtime tests before changing active guidance. If evidence proves the correct solution requires coordinated OpenCode or toolbox work, that work is included through separately tracked repository changes.

## What Changes

- Investigate how Advance authors, generates, deploys, and tests MCP-related instruction prose.
- Test representative runtime combinations with CodeMode enabled and disabled.
- Compare no change, a thin dual-mode bridge, CodeMode-first guidance with fallback, and runtime/generated capability-specific guidance.
- Measure correctness, prompt overhead, maintainability, fallback behavior, and generated/deployed parity.
- Implement only the evidence-supported shape across Advance and any demonstrably required OpenCode/toolbox surfaces.
- Track each affected repository through its own ADV change, branch, verification, and release evidence.

## User Outcomes

- Advance agents invoke available MCP capabilities correctly with CodeMode enabled and disabled.
- Advance guidance does not contradict the active tool surface.
- Exact callable/catalog paths remain protected from normalization errors.
- Advance avoids carrying duplicated runtime syntax that OpenCode already generates authoritatively.
- Maintainers can verify instruction and deployment parity after future tool-surface changes.
- Required cross-repository fixes ship coherently rather than leaving one mode partially broken.

## Affected Code

Primary Advance investigation surfaces:

- `.opencode/agents/*.md`, especially `adv.md` and `adv-researcher.md`
- `.opencode/overlays/*.overlay.md`
- active `.opencode/command/*.md` and `skills/*/SKILL.md` references
- `ADV_INSTRUCTIONS.md` and `SETUP.md`
- `scripts/deploy-local.sh` prompt/overlay generation paths
- `plugin/src/tool-name-assets.test.ts` and related deploy/asset coverage tests

Conditional external surfaces:

- OpenCode CodeMode/tool-registry or plugin-hook surfaces, only if design evidence proves an upstream change is required.
- toolbox `oc` wrapper and backed-up runtime instructions, including any verified mode-toggle defect.

The exact edit set remains a discovery/design outcome. Archived `.adv/archive/**` evidence is read-only historical state and is not an implementation target.

## Related Repositories

- **Advance** — primary owner of guidance, deployment generation, and coverage tests.
- **OpenCode** — owns CodeMode exposure, catalog generation, and exact invocation syntax; changes allowed only when evidence proves a required platform fix.
- **toolbox** — owns the `oc` wrapper and global instruction backups; changes allowed when required for correct mode selection or rollout.

Each repository keeps separate tracked change state and verification while this change coordinates the shared outcome.

## Constraints

- Investigation and representative tests precede broad instruction edits.
- OpenCode remains the authority for exact CodeMode catalog syntax.
- The solution must follow actual exposed capabilities, not infer correctness solely from an environment flag.
- CodeMode and direct-schema operation must both pass acceptance tests.
- Built-in and Advance plugin tool invocation must not be reclassified as MCP behavior.
- Canonical sources, overlays, generated/deployed assets, and tests must remain aligned.
- Cross-repository edits require direct evidence and separate tracked changes; no speculative platform work.

## Impact

Potential impact spans primary and spawned Advance agent prompts plus any required OpenCode/toolbox integration surface. Incorrect guidance can produce unavailable-tool calls; over-correcting can add persistent prompt overhead and fragile coupling to experimental internals. The selected shape therefore affects correctness, context cost, maintainability, compatibility, and rollback across repositories.

Rollback must restore each repository’s prior canonical source and regenerate deployed assets from that source. No live deployed artifact may become an independent source of truth.

## Context

Initial source research and runtime probes found:

- CodeMode substitutes `execute` for directly exposed MCP tools.
- OpenCode already generates exact catalog signatures, discovery instructions, and bracket-notation guidance.
- `execute` availability depends on the final MCP catalog, not only the CodeMode flag.
- CodeMode-on primary and spawned Advance agents successfully invoked `tools.context7["resolve-library-id"]`.
- CodeMode-off Advance successfully invoked direct `context7_resolve-library-id`.
- With all external MCP servers disabled, `execute` was absent; stale Advance prose initially caused a false claim that disabled tools were exposed, while actual invocation correctly reported unavailable.
- Advance’s current system-transform hook receives session ID and system text but not final permission-filtered tool inventory.
- The toolbox mode-disable escape hatch does not clear an already inherited CodeMode variable, a verified conditional external defect.
- `consolidateAdvToolSurface2` may edit overlapping prompt assets and creates a coordination/rebase risk, not a semantic scope conflict.

These findings narrow the options but do not authorize broad implementation before design selects the least-coupled correct mechanism.

## Discovery Agenda

1. Complete the correctness matrix across CodeMode on/off, primary/spawned agent, MCP available/unavailable, and identifier/punctuated tool names.
2. Measure Advance-contributed prompt overhead for viable guidance shapes.
3. Verify canonical, overlay-generated, provider/deployed, and test-fixture parity.
4. Define evidence-based selection criteria for static bridge versus runtime/platform integration.
5. Coordinate with `consolidateAdvToolSurface2` for overlapping prompt assets.
6. Route any required OpenCode/toolbox implementation through separate linked changes.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Advance-specific research, experiments, architecture decision, and evidence-supported instruction/generation/test changes.
- Active source and generated/deployed parity surfaces.
- Verified compatibility with CodeMode-enabled and direct-schema sessions.
- Separately tracked OpenCode/toolbox changes when direct evidence proves they are necessary for the agreed outcome.

### Out of Scope

- Unrelated OpenCode, toolbox, or MCP inventory improvements.
- Redesigning Advance plugin tool registration.
- Editing archived ADV change bundles.
- General tool-context optimization unrelated to invocation correctness.
- Opportunistic platform changes without an acceptance-criterion dependency.

### Must Not

- Must not assume CodeMode is always enabled or that `execute` is always exposed.
- Must not duplicate OpenCode’s full generated MCP catalog in Advance prompts.
- Must not rewrite all concrete references before tests and design establish the selected shape.
- Must not edit deployed artifacts without changing and regenerating their owning source.
- Must not fold external repository work into untracked edits.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Advance will use a **mode-neutral active-surface contract**, not a CodeMode translation layer. OpenCode owns tool exposure and exact CodeMode catalog syntax. Advance contributes one compact invariant to each effective agent prompt that can use external MCP:

> For external MCP capabilities, use only the active tool surface. If `execute` is exposed, follow its generated catalog and exact returned paths. Otherwise use direct MCP callables exactly as exposed. Never infer availability from prose or normalize identifiers; report an absent capability as unavailable.

Workflow prose names capabilities/providers without embedding host-specific callable syntax. Exact MCP permission keys remain valid in YAML frontmatter/configuration. No OpenCode patch or Advance runtime translation hook is planned. A separately tracked toolbox change repairs the inherited CodeMode-disable defect and gates acceptance.

## Key Decisions

1. **Active surface owns availability.** Flags/prose cannot prove a tool exists.
2. **One mode-neutral contract.** OpenCode owns generated paths; Advance owns exact-surface obedience.
3. **Capability prose replaces callable prose.** Durable workflow intent stays; invocation syntax comes from active schema/catalog.
4. **Frontmatter and prompt bodies are distinct.** Parse YAML separately so valid permission keys remain.
5. **Deployment manifest defines active corpus.** Scan recursively deployed agents, overlays, commands, and full skill directories; exclude `.adv/archive/**`.
6. **Test effective assembled prompts.** Exactly one contract per MCP-capable effective agent; no command-level duplication.
7. **No speculative OpenCode work.** Re-enter design only for new reproducible contract blocker.
8. **Toolbox fix gates acceptance.** `OC_DISABLE_CODE_MODE=1` must override inherited CodeMode state through separate tracked work.
9. **Coordinate with `consolidateAdvToolSurface2`.** Inventory overlap and explicitly rebase/merge prompt assets.

## ADR Drafts

None. Reversible prompt/test architecture, not hard-to-reverse platform commitment.

## Implementation Strategy

### A. Advance RED tests

1. Add frontmatter-aware prompt-body extraction.
2. Derive recursive active corpus from deployment ownership, including skill sibling/reference files.
3. Replace tests that positively require concrete direct MCP names in prose.
4. Freeze pre-change effective assembled-prompt fixtures.
5. Add failing assertions for unconditional concrete invocation prose, missing/duplicated contract, altered frontmatter keys, more than 400 added UTF-8 bytes, duplicated catalog signatures, and canonical/overlay/deployed drift.
6. Add explicit runtime rows: CodeMode primary; CodeMode spawned researcher; direct-mode primary; CodeMode/no-MCP; identifier-safe and punctuated paths.

### B. Advance GREEN migration

1. Add compact canonical contract to applicable effective agent surfaces.
2. Replace concrete callable examples in active agent, command, overlay, skill/reference, `ADV_INSTRUCTIONS.md`, and `SETUP.md` prompt prose with capability wording.
3. Preserve exact permission keys in frontmatter/configuration.
4. Regenerate/review deployment-owned assets; leave archives untouched.

### C. Toolbox linked change

1. Create separately tracked toolbox change.
2. Add failing wrapper test for inherited CodeMode variable plus disable escape hatch.
3. Update canonical wrapper source to clear/override inherited state.
4. Deploy canonically, sync non-secret backup, verify both modes.

### D. Integration

1. Reconcile against `consolidateAdvToolSurface2`.
2. Run recursive corpus, effective-prompt, deployment-parity, byte-budget, and runtime-matrix verification.
3. Record linked toolbox release evidence.
4. Keep OpenCode unchanged absent new blocker and design re-entry.

## LBP Analysis

- Machine-exposed capabilities own truth.
- One invariant replaces repeated host syntax and avoids adapter code.
- OpenCode owns syntax; Advance owns workflow intent.
- Same contract covers CodeMode, direct mode, absent MCP, punctuation, primary agents, and spawned researchers.
- Parsed frontmatter, deployment-derived corpus, frozen fixtures, byte budgets, and explicit matrix rows provide structural enforcement.

## Affected Components

### Advance

- `.opencode/agents/*.md`
- `.opencode/overlays/*.overlay.md`
- active `.opencode/command/*.md`
- recursively deployed prompt-bearing `skills/**`
- `ADV_INSTRUCTIONS.md`, `SETUP.md`

- overlay/deploy assembly tests and prompt-corpus helpers

### toolbox

- wrapper tests
- `backups/dotfiles/` source snapshot

### OpenCode

Source/reference evidence only; no planned edits.

## Design-Derived Criteria

- DDC1: Frozen effective-prompt fixtures provide deterministic baselines; guidance adds at most 400 UTF-8 bytes and appears once per applicable prompt.
- DDC2: Active-corpus discovery follows recursive deployment ownership and parses YAML frontmatter separately.
